title: Selenium Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Selenium lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Open a small page
entries.summary: Selenium controls a browser through WebDriver. A data URL can hold a tiny HTML page for a local practice test.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Library

')) assert driver.find_element(By.TAG_NAME, "h1").text == "Library" finally: driver.quit()

notes: Close the driver in finally so a failed check does not leave a browser open.

entries.name: Find by ID
entries.summary: An ID should identify one page element. Selenium can use it to find a control.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<button id="save">Save</button>'))
    assert driver.find_element(By.ID, "save").text == "Save"
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: Two elements should not share the same ID.

entries.name: Find several elements
entries.summary: find_elements returns a list of all matches. It is different from find_element, which returns one match.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('
  • Moon
  • Ocean
')) assert len(driver.find_elements(By.TAG_NAME, "li")) == 2 finally: driver.quit()

notes: An empty result list is different from a single element not being found.

entries.name: Type into an input
entries.summary: send_keys types into an element. Read the value property to see what the field now contains.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<label for="title">Title</label><input id="title">'))
    field = driver.find_element(By.ID, "title")
    field.send_keys("Moon")
    assert field.get_property("value") == "Moon"
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: Element text is not the same as an input's value property.

entries.name: Click and observe
entries.summary: A click asks the browser to activate a control. Check the resulting page state.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<button id="save" onclick="this.textContent=\'Done\'">Save</button>'))
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "save").click()
    assert driver.find_element(By.ID, "save").text == "Done"
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: A click alone does not prove the intended action completed.

entries.name: Use a CSS selector
entries.summary: A CSS selector describes elements by tags, classes or attributes. Keep it short and tied to a clear target.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Ready

')) assert driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "p.notice").text == "Ready" finally: driver.quit()

notes: Long position-based selectors can break after a harmless layout change.

entries.name: Check selected state
entries.summary: A checkbox has a selected state that can be inspected. Clicking toggles that state.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<label><input id="remember" type="checkbox">Remember</label>'))
    box = driver.find_element(By.ID, "remember")
    box.click()
    assert box.is_selected()
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: Check the starting state before using a toggle as a setup step.

entries.name: Choose a select option
entries.summary: Selenium's Select helper handles a native select element. Choose an option by its stored value.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<select id="size"><option value="s">Small</option><option value="l">Large</option></select>'))
    from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import Select
    menu = Select(driver.find_element(By.ID, "size"))
    menu.select_by_value("l")
    assert menu.first_selected_option.text == "Large"
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: The Select helper does not work on a custom menu built from div elements.

entries.name: Wait for a condition
entries.summary: An explicit wait checks for a condition until a time limit. It is more useful than always sleeping a fixed length.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Ready

')) from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC item = WebDriverWait(driver, 5).until(EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "ready"))) assert item.text == "Ready" finally: driver.quit()

notes: Do not use long fixed sleeps to hide a timing problem.

entries.name: Press a keyboard key
entries.summary: Keyboard actions help check access beyond mouse clicks. Tab normally moves focus to the next control.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('<input id="first"><input id="second">'))
    from selenium.webdriver.common.keys import Keys
    first = driver.find_element(By.ID, "first")
    first.click()
    first.send_keys(Keys.TAB)
    assert driver.switch_to.active_element.get_attribute("id") == "second"
finally:
    driver.quit()

notes: A keyboard test should check the focused element, not just send a key.

entries.name: Find an element again after change
entries.summary: A page can replace a DOM element. A saved old element reference may then be stale, so locate the current element again.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Old

')) driver.find_element(By.ID, "replace").click() assert driver.find_element(By.ID, "message").text == "New" finally: driver.quit()

notes: Do not retry the same stale object forever; find the current element.

entries.name: Save evidence and close
entries.summary: A screenshot helps show what the browser displayed. Always release browser resources when a test ends.

example.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Library

')) assert driver.find_element(By.TAG_NAME, "h1").is_displayed() driver.save_screenshot("library.png") finally: driver.quit()

notes: A screenshot supplements assertions; it does not check every hidden rule.
